text.title: AI-Assisted Accessibility Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules grounding the ai-assisted-accessibility methodology plus the `skip-this-methodology` safety rule. Each rule pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale. Background: AI-powered accessibility tools by category, integration points across the development lifecycle, and capability comparison for 2026. Also the 5-stage pipeline from automated scan to user validation, including the human-AI responsibility split and ROI data.

section.title: Background

list.item: axe DevTools Pro — AI suggestions, issue prioritization, fix chatbot; $$$
Deque axe Enterprise — intelligent false-positive reduction, AI fix recommendations; $$$
Level Access — Ask Level AI chatbot for WCAG Q&A; no programmatic scan API; $$$
Evinced — AI-powered continuous testing; REST API for CI/CD integration; $$$
Siteimprove — enterprise monitoring with AI trend analysis; REST API; $$$
AudioEye — AI remediation with human oversight; not overlay-based; $$
Accessibility Insights (Microsoft) — code fix recommendations, automated guidance; free
WAVE — visual feedback with annotations; free browser extension
Lighthouse — performance + a11y scoring with AI insights; free (Chrome DevTools)
Stark — contrast checking, vision simulation, AI suggestions; free/$
axe-playwright — headless WCAG scanning in CI; OSS
pa11y-ci — batch URL scanning in CI pipelines; OSS
jest-axe — unit-level accessibility assertions; OSS
eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y — static JSX a11y linting; OSS
Design: Figma (Stark plugin), Adobe XD (built-in checker), Sketch (contrast plugins)
Development: VS Code (axe Linter), JetBrains (inspections), ESLint (jsx-a11y), Storybook (a11y addon)
Testing: Playwright (axe-playwright), Cypress (cypress-axe), Jest (jest-axe)
CI/CD: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI (pa11y), Jenkins, CircleCI
Issue-level AI: tools attached to individual audit issues; one-click fix suggestions without context switching
VPAT generation: draft in seconds vs. hours of manual work
False positive reduction: 30–40% down to 10–15%
In-IDE hints: VS Code and JetBrains real-time a11y linting
Alt text generators: Azure Computer Vision, Google Vision AI, OpenAI GPT-4V, Claude
Caption tools: 3Play Media (AI + human, 99% accuracy), Rev.ai (80–90%)

section.p: 5-stage pipeline (the procedure in 04-procedure.xml expands stages 1-2 into the two-model split and adds stages 3-5 as steps 4-7):

list.item: 1. Automated Scan: run axe, WAVE, Lighthouse; AI prioritizes findings; false positives filtered (10–15% remain)
2. AI Suggestions: review AI-proposed code fixes; understand why issue matters; get multiple fix options ranked by best practice
3. Manual Verification: test keyboard navigation; verify logical fix makes sense; check edge cases AI missed
4. User Testing: test with people with disabilities using real assistive technology; validate AI assumptions
5. Continuous Monitoring: AI scans on every deploy; track trends over time; alert on new critical issues
AI: repetitive scanning, code extraction, report generation, WCAG Q&A, draft alt text, priority ranking, regression testing
Human: context and empathy in content decisions, complex judgment calls, user testing, strategic fix decisions, edge cases, final review, accessibility culture
Manual audit: 20–40 hours; $5,000–$20,000 per audit
AI-assisted audit: 5–10 hours; 60–75% time reduction
AI tools: $100–$2,000/month; break-even at 1–3 audits/year
Manual only: 50–70% issue detection; AI + Manual: 85–95%
Continuous AI: prevents 40% of issues before production

rule.statement: The pipeline MUST use a Haiku-class model for scan + filter + rank AND a Sonnet-class model for fix generation. Using one model for both is forbidden.

rationale.source: Internal — model-routing policy + AI accessibility 2026 audits

rule.rationale: Haiku is cheap+fast for the mechanical filter; Sonnet is needed for the judgment in fix generation. Mixing them wastes cost (Sonnet on filtering) or quality (Haiku on fixes).

rule.statement: Every AI output (filtered issue list, fix proposal, alt text batch) MUST be reviewed by a human accessibility expert before any developer ticket is created. AI-direct-to-backlog is forbidden.

rationale.source: WCAG audit best practices + Internal — validation policy

rule.rationale: Without expert validation, AI false positives flood the backlog and erode developer trust in the whole pipeline.

rule.statement: Critical paths (auth, checkout, search) MUST be scanned by at least two tools (axe + pa11y) and the union of violations passed to the AI filter.
rule.rationale: Single-tool scans miss tool-specific blind spots; cross-checking critical paths catches violations only one tool sees.

rule.statement: Every AI-generated fix MUST cite the WCAG success criterion (e.g., `2.4.4 Link Purpose`) and the file:line it patches. Unanchored fixes are rejected.
rule.rationale: Fixes without WCAG citation drift from spec; without file:line they cannot be merged.

rule.statement: Bulk alt-text generation MUST be throttled to N images per batch (typical N=50) with an expert sample review of ≥ 10% of each batch.
rule.rationale: Unlimited bulk + zero review produces drift in tone + accuracy; throttling + sampling is the defensible middle.

rule.statement: AI handles repetitive scanning and report generation; humans handle all contextual decisions and user testing validation.
rule.rationale: AI finds issues faster and more consistently; humans provide context, empathy, and judgment. Combining both produces 85–95% issue coverage vs 50–70% for manual alone.

rule.statement: Scan new pages on every deployment, not just periodically — regressions appear silently.
rule.rationale: New code regularly introduces accessibility regressions. One-time audits miss regressions introduced between audits. CI-integrated scanning catches them at the source.

rule.statement: Skip this methodology when the preconditions in `## Applies If` are not all true, or any item in `## Skip If` holds. The decision tree routes to this rule on those branches.
rule.rationale: A methodology that runs on the wrong input wastes tokens and produces misleading artifacts. The explicit skip rule is the safety valve.
